title: SaaS Platforms Every Architecture Enthusiast Should Know
description: Discover essential SaaS platforms for architecture enthusiasts, from 3D modeling to project management. Learn about architecture passion, degrees, and digital resources.
body_html:
Fellow architecture enthusiasts will agree - it's challenging to stay current with innovative tools and resources for architectural design and planning.

The good news is, with the right SaaS platforms, you can unlock a world of possibilities for your architectural passions and projects.

In this post, we will explore some of the most useful SaaS tools available today for architecture modeling, collaboration, project management, inspiration, and more. You'll discover solutions to enhance every step of realizing your creative visions, from conception to construction.

Introduction to SaaS Platforms for Architects and Enthusiasts

SaaS (Software as a Service) platforms provide cloud-based access to software applications, removing the need to install programs directly onto local devices. For architecture enthusiasts, SaaS opens up convenient access to powerful design, planning, collaboration, and analysis tools without expensive upfront investments.

The Evolution of Architecture Software via SaaS

In the past, architects were limited to desktop programs like AutoCAD for drafting and design work. The shift to cloud-based services has enabled new possibilities:

  • Access design software anywhere via web browsers on any device
  • Centralized storage allowing seamless collaboration
  • Regular automated updates with new features
  • Flexible subscription plans rather than large upfront license fees

For enthusiasts, SaaS unlocks sophisticated architecture software that was previously inaccessible or cost-prohibitive.

Overview of Architecture Planning Platforms

Later sections will explore leading SaaS tools in areas like 3D modeling, project management, and generative design. Key platforms to be covered include:

  • SketchUp - Intuitive 3D modeling and drafting
  • CoConstruct - Construction project management
  • Enscape - Photorealistic renderings and VR walkthroughs
  • Morpholio - Concept sketching and collaboration

These services represent the vanguard of architecture SaaS, offering robust feature sets tailored specifically for architecture enthusiasts and professionals.

What is an architecture person called?

An architect is a person who plans, designs and oversees the construction of buildings.

To practice architecture means to provide services in connection with the design of buildings and the space within the site surrounding the buildings that have human occupancy or use as their principal purpose.

In summary, an architect is a professional who specializes in the art and science of building design. They work with clients to determine goals, requirements and budget for a construction project, develop the overall layout and aesthetic, produce drawings and documents for contractors, obtain permits, and oversee the building process through to completion.

What is the passion of an architect?

Passion is essential for architects because it drives creativity, innovation, and commitment to their work. Architecture is an incredibly demanding career that requires intense focus, dedication to detail, and a willingness to devote extensive time to projects. Without a true passion for design and the built environment, it would be difficult to find the motivation needed to thrive.

Some key reasons why passion matters in architecture include:

  • Creativity: Architecture is an outlet for creative expression and vision. Passion fuels the imagination and enables architects to develop inspired, unique design concepts. It pushes the boundaries of what is possible.
  • Problem-Solving: Architects must find thoughtful solutions to complex spatial and structural challenges. A passion for design promotes persistence in working through these problems to achieve optimal, integrated results.
  • Attention to Detail: The difference between a good building and an exceptional building often lies in the finer details. An architect's passion and perfectionism lead to more meticulous, thoughtful design.
  • Commitment: Architectural projects require immense investments of time, care, and dedicated focus over extended periods. Passion provides the energy and drive needed to fully commit to a project from start to finish.
  • Connection to Purpose: Passion strengthens an architect's connection to their higher purpose - to positively shape the built environment and improve people's quality of life through design. This provides meaning and fulfillment.

In short, passion is the beating heart that pumps life and soul into architectural design. It uplifts a career of practical challenges into a creatively fulfilling vocation driven by vision and meaning. Passion is what separates the most influential, inspiring architects from the average. It is the essential foundation for advancing the art and impact of architecture.

Why does architecture interest people?

Architecture is fascinating because it combines art, science, and engineering to create beautiful and functional spaces. Here are a few key reasons why architecture captivates many:

  • Creative Expression - Architects enjoy the creative process of designing unique buildings and spaces. They get to imagine and draw their ideas, experimenting with different shapes, materials, layouts and more to achieve their desired aesthetic. It's an incredibly rewarding creative outlet.
  • Problem Solving - Architecture requires finding innovative solutions to complex spatial and structural challenges. Determining how to configure spaces and support massive buildings while meeting client needs and constraints involves complex yet rewarding problem solving.
  • Artistry - Many architects appreciate architecture's fusion of art and design. They take pride in crafting visually stunning structures from the smallest details to the grand exterior form. Quality architecture can be appreciated as an art form.
  • Storytelling - The best buildings capture something about their locale, purpose or time period through conscious design choices. Architects enjoy shaping spaces that will tell a meaningful story to occupants and visitors for decades or centuries.
  • Improving Lives - Knowing their buildings will be part of communities and positively impact people can be very motivating for architects. Thoughtful design promotes health, productivity, connection and quality of life.
  • Passion - Most architects simply have a lifelong passion for the built environment and their role in creating it. Their enthusiasm for imagining and making functional art keeps the profession going strong.

What do you call someone with an architecture degree?

Most people that complete a degree in architecture typically use one of the following titles:

  • Architect-in-training (AIT)
  • Designer
  • Architectural designer
  • Associate

The most common title used is "architect-in-training" (AIT). This indicates the individual has completed their architecture degree but still needs to gain practical experience and pass further licensing exams before being fully certified as an architect.

An AIT works under the supervision of a licensed architect to gain hands-on training. Once they meet eligibility requirements for licensure - which varies by region - they can take the Architect Registration Examination (ARE) or other exams. Upon passing and meeting experience thresholds, AITs finally earn the title "architect" and can practice independently.

So in summary, while someone with an architecture degree has strong educational foundations, until fully licensed the appropriate titles are AIT, designer, architectural designer, or associate. The titles signal ongoing progress toward full professional certification.

Virtual Design Software for Architectural Modeling

This section will cover popular SaaS platforms that enable architecture enthusiasts to create 3D building models and experiment with innovative digital design techniques.

SketchUp - User-Friendly 3D Modeling for Architecture

SketchUp is a versatile 3D modeling software that is popular among architecture enthusiasts for its intuitive and easy-to-use interface. With SketchUp, users can quickly create detailed 3D models of buildings, experiment with different architectural designs, and even integrate their models into professional architecture, engineering and construction (AEC) workflows.

Some key features that make SketchUp ideal for architecture enthusiasts include:

  • Drag-and-drop modeling tools to easily "pull" and sculpt geometric shapes into 3D forms.
  • An extensive 3D model library containing over 250,000 free building models to customize.
  • Support for importing CAD files and GIS data to use as a starting point for modeling.
  • Dynamic components that can intelligently adapt to changes, saving time.
  • Built-in access to Google Earth and Maps for placing designs into real-world contexts.
  • A robust extension library that adds specialized tools for architecture workflows like BIM modeling, rendering, construction documentation, etc.

With its focus on usability and architecture-specific features, SketchUp provides a great entry point into 3D modeling for architecture enthusiasts looking to bring their building designs to life.

Revit Cloud - BIM and CAD Software for Architects

For architecture enthusiasts interested in more advanced building information modeling (BIM) techniques, Autodesk's Revit Cloud offers access to professional-grade architectural design and collaboration tools through an affordable software as a service (SaaS) model.

Revit Cloud gives users full access to Revit's powerful BIM platform to create rich architectural models with intelligent components, analyze building performance, automatically create construction drawings, and coordinate with other project stakeholders in the cloud.

Key features relevant for architecture enthusiasts include:

  • Import architectural CAD files as a starting point for modeling.
  • Highly visual and intuitive 3D modeling environment.
  • Vast component libraries for architectural elements like doors, windows, walls, etc.
  • Tools for analyzing sunlight, thermal performance, and other metrics.
  • Auto-generated floor plans, sections, elevations drawings.
  • Cloud collaboration for working with other enthusiasts and professionals.

By leveraging Revit's professional BIM capabilities on a flexible SaaS platform, architecture enthusiasts can take their designs to the next level without the overhead of managing complex desktop software.

Morpholio - Creative Architectural Design Tools

Morpholio offers architecture enthusiasts an innovative suite of mobile and desktop apps tailored for the conceptual stages of architectural design. From quick sketching to diagramming, Morpholio facilitates creative exploration and visual communication of architectural ideas.

Key features of Morpholio for architecture enthusiasts include:

  • An intuitive sketching app offering a range of drawing tools for getting ideas on "paper".
  • Diagram mode to map out relationships between spaces and components.
  • Customizable canvas with CAD/BIM integration to combine digital and hand-drawn elements.
  • Augmented reality that overlays sketches onto real-world camera views for contextualizing designs.
  • Cloud-based collaboration and presentation tools.

With its focus on supporting early-stage design thinking rather than detailed technical drawing, Morpholio offers architecture enthusiasts an ideal platform for having fun experimenting with architectural concepts and sharing visionary ideas with clients or collaborators.

Collaboration and Architecture Project Management in the Cloud

This section explores SaaS platforms that facilitate collaboration, communication, and project management for architecture teams.

BIM 360 - Comprehensive Cloud Services for Architecture

BIM 360 offers a comprehensive set of cloud-based collaboration and data management tools tailored for architecture, engineering and construction teams. Key features include:

  • Centralized access to BIM models, documents, and project data
  • Advanced model coordination to reduce clashes and rework
  • Automated workflows for submittals, RFIs, and change orders
  • Mobile capabilities for onsite access and coordination
  • Analytics dashboards to track project performance

By consolidating project information into a common data environment, BIM 360 enables seamless collaboration between all project stakeholders - from architects and engineers to contractors and owners. Its specialized toolset streamlines communication and improves visibility across design, pre-construction, and construction phases.

For architecture enthusiasts seeking robust BIM-centric SaaS platforms, BIM 360 delivers enterprise-grade functionality with the flexibility of the cloud. Its tight integration with Autodesk's Revit and Civil 3D also provides a smooth roundtrip workflow between models and project management tools.

Procore - Online Architecture Tools for Construction Management

While Procore targets the construction phase, it offers some unique capabilities for architects involved in project delivery. Key features relevant to architecture teams include:

  • Powerful quality and safety tools
  • Comprehensive financial controls
  • Document management for submittals and RFIs
  • Daily field reports and construction photos
  • Punch lists and project closeout workflows

Procore gives architects transparency into onsite construction progress and communication through daily field reports, photos, and document workflows. Its quality management tools also facilitate defect tracking and resolution between the architect and contractor.

For architects that want better visibility after bid or those involved in construction administration services, Procore delivers the field-tested tools to smooth collaboration with contractors.

Viewpoint - Architecture Planning Platforms for Efficiency

Viewpoint offers core construction project management tools tailored for owners, contractors, and architects alike. Capabilities most relevant to architecture teams include:

  • Intuitive project planning and scheduling
  • Complete budget management functionalities
  • Streamlined submittals, RFIs, and change order workflows
  • Automated field reports for tracking jobsite activity
  • Punch list and closeout management

It covers the full spectrum - from early planning and budgeting to onsite construction visibility and closeout. Viewpoint enables architects to effectively collaborate with project owners and contractors throughout design and construction.

Its flexible platform and reasonable pricing also make it an attractive choice for small and mid-sized architecture firms. For streamlined project delivery, Viewpoint brings excellent value.

Digital Resources for Architects: Research and Inspiration

Architecture enthusiasts can leverage a variety of SaaS platforms to conduct research and find design inspiration. From discovering notable projects worldwide to sourcing products and materials, these digital resources offer invaluable insight.

Architecture Helper: Unleashing Creativity and Analysis

Architecture Helper is a groundbreaking platform designed to foster a deeper understanding and appreciation of architectural styles and influences. By allowing users to submit photographs of buildings for instant architectural analysis, the platform offers insights into the elements that define various architectural designs. It's an educational and explorative tool that caters to architecture students, hobbyists, and enthusiasts alike, enabling them to:

  • Receive instant analysis and insights on user-submitted building images.
  • Explore a rich library of real building analyses to understand different architectural styles and influences.
  • Mix and match architectural elements to generate new designs, facilitating a hands-on approach to learning and creativity.

Whether you're looking to identify the styles and influences in your own photography or eager to experiment with design combinations, Architecture Helper provides a unique platform for discovery and innovation in architecture.

WikiArquitectura: A Comprehensive Architectural Encyclopedia

WikiArquitectura serves as an extensive encyclopedia of architecture, offering detailed information on a wide array of projects from around the globe. This platform is invaluable for architects, students, and enthusiasts seeking to deepen their knowledge and find inspiration. Features include:

  • Detailed project profiles encompassing architectural plans, sections, and elevations, alongside comprehensive descriptions.
  • A vast collection of architectural works, categorized by types, styles, and geography, making it easy to research and discover new projects.
  • An educational resource for understanding the technical and creative aspects of notable buildings and structures.

WikiArquitectura is an essential tool for anyone looking to explore the world of architecture further, offering insights into the design principles and techniques behind some of the most iconic buildings.

Archello - Discovering Architecture Projects Online

Archello serves as an extensive database for discovering architecture projects from around the world. Key features include:

  • Searchable directory of over 44,000 building projects globally
  • Detailed project profiles with images, architects, materials used and more
  • Ability to save favorite projects and follow leading architecture firms
  • Daily digest of latest published projects in your inbox

Whether researching a specific building technique or browsing for inspiration, Archello allows architecture enthusiasts to digitally explore an impressive catalog of realized projects.

Architizer - A Search Engine for Architectural Innovation

Architizer operates as a search engine tailored specifically for architecture and design. It provides access to:

  • Over 500,000 building products from 4,000+ manufacturers
  • Directory of top architecture firms from across the globe
  • Database of notable architecture projects searchable by location, building type and more

For sourcing building materials or discovering innovative firms leading the way globally, Architizer makes researching architecture simple and engaging.

Houzz - A Portal for Interior Design and Architectural Ideas

Houzz offers a vibrant community showcasing beautiful home design and architecture. Its features include:

  • Millions of high-quality home design photos and articles
  • Curated home design ideas spanning every style
  • Direct access to top architects and building professionals

Whether seeking inspiration on the latest interior design trends or sourcing products for a home renovation, Houzz provides architecture enthusiasts an ideal portal for ideas and solutions.

These digital platforms demonstrate how modern SaaS solutions are empowering architecture enthusiasts with valuable resources for research, discovery and design inspiration. From accessing a global catalog of projects to connecting with industry experts, the options for exploration are virtually endless.

Conclusion: Integrating SaaS into Your Architectural Practice

This concluding section will summarize key takeaways and provide suggestions for readers to continue expanding their knowledge of essential architecture SaaS platforms.

Recap of Essential Online Architecture Tools

A recap of the top SaaS recommendations covered previously based on common enthusiast needs around 3D modeling, project management, and research:

  • SketchUp - A versatile and intuitive 3D modeling software for architecture enthusiasts to visualize and share building designs. Offers a library of models and textures to easily create realistic building visualizations.
  • Asana - A flexible project management platform to organize inspiration, reference materials, and project plans. Great for collaborating with team members on building designs.
  • Architizer - A discovery platform to research architectural styles and be inspired by top projects from around the world. Filled with examples for enthusiasts seeking ideas.

Furthering Your Architecture Enthusiasm with Advanced SaaS Platforms

Tips for enthusiasts to keep exploring niche architecture SaaS tools for specialized needs from landscaping to sustainability evaluation:

  • Consider landscape architecture tools like Land F/X for realistic 3D site modeling and visualization.
  • Evaluate building sustainability with energy analysis software such as Sefaira and EnergyPlus.
  • Explore virtual reality platforms like IrisVR to create immersive walkthroughs of building designs.
  • Use rendering engines like Enscape to create hyperrealistic visualizations with dynamic lighting and rich materials.

Continuously expanding your SaaS toolkit will open up new creative possibilities in your architecture projects and enthusiasm.
